_note: Returns all users on the n8n instance. Combined with workflow shared[] data, this gives ownership mapping without manual assignment.
_llm_can_infer: How many people work with automations in this company
Who is the instance owner (likely the main automation person or IT lead)
Whether there are pending invites (team growth / onboarding signal)
Combined with workflow shared[].role: who OWNS which workflows — deterministic ownership
Bus factor: if 1 user owns 15 of 18 workflows, that's a concentration risk
Team structure: admin vs member distribution shows how centralized automation responsibility is
Activity: createdAt/updatedAt shows when users were added — recent additions = growing automation team

_business_value.ownership_mapping: Expliq currently requires manual owner assignment. With users + shared[] data, we can auto-assign owners from n8n. 'Sarah Chen owns 6 workflows' becomes a FACT.
_business_value.bus_factor_analysis: If 1 person owns 80% of workflows, that's a governance risk Expliq should surface. The Automation Intelligence page can say: 'Your automation knowledge is concentrated in 1 person — consider cross-training.'
_business_value.team_size_signal: Number of n8n users hints at automation team size. 2 users = small team. 10 users = dedicated automation function. This informs the LLM's company analysis.
_business_value.pending_users: isPending=true means invited but haven't accepted. Could indicate team transition or onboarding issues.
